articles.title: ‘Sanitation workers live 11 years less than professionals’
articles.summary: IIPS study: India’s sanitation workers live 11.4 years less than professionals, face toxic exposure, high health costs, low insurance; calls for mechanisation.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s sanitation workers have an estimated life expectancy of 63.8 years, nearly 11.4 years less than professional and managerial workers. Urban male sanitation workers have a life expectancy that is lower than their women counterparts, a study by the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS) has found.The study, Bridging the Life Expectancy Gap of Sanitation Workers in India, found that sanitation workers live 9.6 years less than agricultural and manual workers, indicating that poverty and economic disadvantage alone may not explain the gap.For urban centres such as Delhi, the study found that the usual life-expectancy advantage associated with city living does not extend to sanitation workers. Urban male sanitation workers have an estimated life expectancy of just 62.3 years, while urban women sanitation workers have an estimated life expectancy of 64.3 years.Occupational hazards appear to be a significant concern. Around 30.2% of recorded deaths among sanitation workers were classified as poisoning, compared with 5.4% among other occupational groups. The report points to the risks of exposure to toxic gases, particularly during work in sewers, drains and other confined spaces.The financial burden is equally severe.The findings stress the need to treat sanitation-worker safety as a public health priority, particularly in India’s rapidly urbanising cities.Out-of-pocket healthcare spending accounts for 17.4% of the monthly household consumption expenditure among sanitation workers, the highest proportion across occupational groups. Only 1% of their survey records showed payment of a health insurance premium.The urban disadvantage is also reflected in healthcare costs. Sanitation workers are the only occupational group in the study for whom living in a city does not reduce the risk of catastrophic health expenditure. The proportion of urban sanitation-worker household records crossing the specified health-spending threshold was 7.4%, against 7% in rural areas.The study by IIPS, supported by corporate partners, estimates 77,458 years of potential life lost per 100,000 sanitation workers due to premature mortality, 2.72 times the rate among professional and managerial workers.It also estimates around 128 occupational-hazard-related deaths annually across the country’s sanitation workforce.It calls for greater mechanisation of hazardous sanitation work, stricter workplace safety enforcement, protective equipment, improved healthcare and wider insurance coverage.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: 37,700 gallons of sewage spill into San Diego waterways after pipeline failure; Dog Beach closes over contamination fears; harmful bacteria and viruses could make people and pets seriously ill
articles.summary: Nearly 37,700 gallons of wastewater spilled into waterways connected to the Pacific Ocean near San Diego after a pipeline failure, prompting health
articles.body: Nearly 37,700 gallons of wastewater spilled into waterways connected to the Pacific Ocean near San Diego after a pipeline failure, prompting health warnings and a closure at Ocean Beach's Dog Beach. The incident has raised concerns about exposure to harmful bacteria and viruses, with officials cautioning that contaminated water could make people and pets seriously ill.The spill occurred on Thursday night near Mission Trails Regional Park after a mechanical failure at a newly installed pipeline connection, according to the Padre Dam Municipal Water District. Officials initially estimated that around 160,000 gallons had escaped, but later revised the maximum volume to 37,700 gallons.The contamination led to a water closure at Dog Beach in Ocean Beach, although some visitors appeared unaware of the warning and continued spending time near the water.Health officials warn of bacteria and viruses in contaminated waterRomina Schiess, a supervising environmental health specialist with the county, warned that exposure to wastewater could pose a serious health risk to both people and animals."It carries a lot of contaminants, a lot of bacteria, a lot of viruses, and it can cause people and, in this case, pets to become ill," she told CBS.Health officials have urged beachgoers to pay attention to closure notices and avoid contact with potentially contaminated water. Dogs are also at risk if they swim in or drink affected water.The incident left some visitors surprised by the warning. Stephanie, a tourist from Portugal, told CBS that she had been watching a friend's dog wade into the water without realising there had been a sewage spill."They're tiny, they're yellow, I mean, I didn't see them, no," she said, referring to the warning signs.County officials believe the contamination is unlikely to travel farther down the coast because bacteria begin dying in saltwater.San Diego residents have raised concerns over recurring sewage spillsThe latest incident is likely to bring back concerns among San Diego residents about wastewater contamination and beach water quality. Previous online discussions, including posts on Reddit, have featured complaints about discoloured ocean water after storms and concerns about sewage plumes near Coronado, Imperial Beach and La Jolla.Dog Beach has also faced an earlier closure following an 18,000-gallon wastewater spill, adding to local frustration over repeated contamination incidents.Another major wastewater spill recently hit Long BeachSan Diego's latest incident comes weeks after a separate sewage spill in Belmont Shore, Long Beach, during Halloween weekend. A ruptured sewer pipe released approximately 29,000 gallons of wastewater, with around 14,000 gallons flowing directly into the ocean.The spill prompted Long Beach officials to temporarily close all 15 open coastal swimming areas. articles.title: Cardiff Welsh cake business calls out racist abuse of staff
articles.summary: Adam El Tagoury calls out "disgusting comments" made about his Cardiff Bakehouse staff on TikTok.
articles.body:
The owner of a viral bakery has called out the racist abuse his staff have been subjected to online.

Adam El Tagoury, 46, owns Cardiff Bakehouse in Cardiff Market, which has attracted visitors including actor Stanley Tucci , and regularly shares videos of his busy staff on social media.

In a viral TikTok video, he named and shamed people who made "vile" remarks questioning whether his staff with Asian heritage should be making traditional Welsh products.

He said he has a "duty to protect these girls" and it should not matter where someone is from if "you're good at what you do".

Tagoury said: "It just it just makes you angry, doesn't it? Why do people want to be like that?

"They're keyboard warriors and they sit behind the desk. They just want to try and make themselves feel better by running somebody else into the ground."

Tagoury said he knows the "lovely ladies" who work for him have seen the comments and they are "very private people".

In his TikTok response to one comment, he said: "Most of our staff are British, we ain't prejudice here.

"They're my grandma's recipe, we use local producers, local suppliers, doesn't matter whose making them, it's all about what's going in them and how they're produced.

"I have a fantastic team here who I am extremely proud of."

He added: "I'm here to provide opportunities for anybody who has a right to work here.

"My father is an immigrant. Came here in 1978 from Libya. He's the one who founded this business and I'm obviously, you know, the son of an immigrant.

"I want these people who work for me, who maybe of a minority class, to know that I got their backs."

He said people making racist remarks online "haven't been shy about taking pot-shots at people who are not around to defend themselves".

"So I think we have every right to call these individuals out, call their usernames out, if they want to say those things, then they should be willing to take the effect that's going to come their way," he added.

Tagoury said he does not want the business of people making comments such as these online.

This year, his businesses had a visit from Stanley Tucci, who "looked very happy" while trying some of his Welsh cakes as part of a new TV series.

US food reviewer Kalani Smith, who goes by Kalani Ghost Hunter online and racks up millions of views, said Cardiff Bakehouse's Welsh cakes were "absolutely incredible" and "one of the highlights of the trip".

Race Council Cymru said it was "appalled" by the reports the business had faced criticism questioning whether its products were genuinely Welsh because of the ethnic background of its owners.

"We believe this raises an important question about how we understand Welsh identity and belonging in modern Wales," said chief executive Prof Uzo Iwobi.

"Welsh traditions and cultural heritage should be celebrated and shared by everyone, regardless of their ethnicity or background.

"We stand in support of this business and hope this incident provides an opportunity to celebrate the positive contribution that ethnic minority businesses and communities make to Wales."

In the 2021 census, 93.8% of people in Wales identified as white, down from 95.6% a decade earlier, with the country's overall population growing by 1.4% to 3,107,500.

The proportion identifying as Asian, Asian Welsh or Asian British, the next highest group in the survey, rose from 2.3% to 2.9%.

Mixed or multiple ethnic groups rose from 1% to 1.6%, and those identifying as black, black Welsh, black British, Caribbean or African rose from 0.6% to 0.9%.

articles.title: An Iowa couple planned to divide their farms equally among four children, but a 2003 will gave their son 477.5 acres and each daughter 107.83 acres; the state’s top court has now ordered a challenge to the will dismissed
articles.summary: An Iowa couple planned to divide their farms equally among their four children, but a 2003 will gave their son 477.5 acres and each daughter 107.83 acres.
articles.body: An Iowa couple planned to divide their farms equally among their four children, but a 2003 will gave their son 477.5 acres and each daughter 107.83 acres. The Iowa Supreme Court has now ordered a challenge to that will dismissed, according to the court’s opinion and Justia U.S. Law.The case, In the Matter of the Estate of Lorraine Schultz, turned on a strict probate deadline. The court held that a will contest filed nearly five years after the will was admitted to probate came too late, even though the family had earlier tried to settle the dispute through an agreement.How the will changedCloy and Lorraine Schultz owned several farm properties in northeast Iowa. In 1998, they signed mirror image wills that gave the surviving spouse a life estate and split the remainder equally among their four children, Blaine, Jacquelyn, Annette, and Deborah.After Cloy died, Lorraine made a new will in July 2003. That will gave four farms totaling 420 acres to Blaine, three farms totaling 151 shared acres to the three daughters, and one farm totaling 230 shared acres to all four children.Under that plan, Blaine would receive 477.5 acres, while each daughter would receive 107.83 acres. The will named Blaine and Annette as executors, and Blaine and Deborah as attorneys in fact.What the family did nextThe daughters learned about the 2003 will around 2014. They confronted Blaine, and the four children then consulted an attorney about restoring the 1998 will.The attorney found that Lorraine lacked testamentary capacity. With Lorraine unable to change the 2003 will, the children signed a family settlement agreement in July 2014 that divided the farms equally. Deborah died in 2015 and Blaine died in 2017, before Lorraine. Lorraine died on January 11, 2019, and Annette opened probate later that month.What the court foundThe 2003 will was admitted to probate on January 29, 2019. Notice was mailed to beneficiaries on February 11, and the second newspaper publication appeared on February 13.Under Iowa Code section 633.309, a will contest had to be filed by June 2019. The plaintiffs did not file their challenge until June 2024, nearly five years later.The Iowa Supreme Court rejected arguments that the family settlement agreement paused or restarted the deadline. The court said the statute contains no tolling or equitable exception once a will has been admitted to probate.Why the appeal failedThe plaintiffs argued that the will was not operative when first filed because the family settlement agreement was filed at the same time. They said the will only became relevant after the agreement was found unenforceable in 2024.The Supreme Court disagreed. It said that neither the existence, filing, nor later invalidation of a family settlement agreement tolls or restarts the deadline for contesting a will.The court also said the plaintiffs could have filed a timely will contest and then asked the court to stay it while the settlement agreement was resolved. They could also have sought written joinder from the non signing successors.What the ruling meansThe Iowa Supreme Court vacated the Court of Appeals decision and reversed the district court’s ruling. The case was remanded for dismissal of the will contest.The decision reinforces the importance of probate deadlines. It also shows how a family settlement agreement, even if later invalidated, does not automatically preserve a challenge to a will.For families dealing with estates, the case is a reminder that timing matters. A will contest must be filed within the legal window, regardless of what the parties may have intended or agreed to privately.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Tehran threatens to 'break legs' as 'Trump corridor' prepares to launch on Iran's border
articles.summary: Armenia launches the U.S.-backed Trump Route corridor despite Iran's stark warning it would "break their legs" if Trump crossed its red line.
articles.body: Armenia is set to launch a U.S.-backed transportation and energy project along Iran's northern border Monday, despite warnings from a senior Iranian official that Tehran would "break their legs" if President Donald Trump and his allies crossed the Islamic Republic's "red line." Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan confirmed that the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project would launch Monday, advancing the plan to connect mainland Azerbaijan with its Nakhchivan exclave through southern Armenia and establish energy links with Turkey and Azerbaijan, Turkish media reported, citing Interfax. The project, a centerpiece of a U.S.-brokered peace initiative between Armenia and Azerbaijan, would also expand American economic involvement in the South Caucasus, where Iran has warned against any development it believes could threaten its security or regional influence. TRUMP'S FIRST IRAN WAR ESCALATION POST-MIDTERM LOSSES SEEKS TO CHOKE OFF TEHRAN’S TRADE The corridor has also gained strategic significance amid the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, as Tehran seeks to secure its northern trade routes and limit the U.S. security presence near its borders while Washington maintains its naval blockade and Task Force Iron Gate focuses on Iran's borders. Speaking at the DigiTec 2026 technology conference in Yerevan, Pashinyan said the new TRIPP initiative, also known as the "Trump Corridor," would strengthen Armenia's regional energy connections, according to Interfax. "Tomorrow we will officially announce the launch of the TRIPP program, and energy and electricity transit will be an important component of it," Pashinyan said during a public discussion on artificial intelligence. "We will now connect our network to the electricity grids of Türkiye and Azerbaijan," he added. The announcement followed a warning from Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior foreign policy adviser to Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who accused Armenia of disregarding Tehran's security concerns over the proposed route. "I told the Armenian ambassador the final word, clearly, that if Trump and his allies want to cross this Iranian red line, we will break their legs," Velayati wrote in a Nov. 5 article published by the Iranian newspaper Ettelaat, according to Iran's Tasnim News Agency. TRUMP RETALIATES AFTER IRAN ATTACK AS EXPERT WARNS REGIME IS GROWING MORE DANGEROUS Velayati also warned that Iran would defend its security interests in the South Caucasus regardless of Russia's involvement, pointing to Tehran's longstanding opposition to the proposed route. The roughly 26-mile corridor would run through Armenia's southern Syunik province, near the Iranian border, connecting mainland Azerbaijan to Nakhchivan and providing an onward link to Turkey, a NATO member. The route would include railways, roads, electricity transmission lines and fiber-optic cables, creating trade connections between Central Asia and Europe. Iran has long opposed proposals for what Azerbaijan calls the "Zangezur Corridor," particularly arrangements that Tehran fears could weaken Armenia's control over the territory, disrupt Iran's access to Armenia or expand the presence of outside powers near its borders. In August 2025, Velayati had already warned that the corridor could become a "graveyard" for what he called Trump's mercenaries, according to Al Jazeera. "Such a corridor will turn into a graveyard of the mercenaries of Donald Trump, not a route owned by the U.S. president," Velayati said, according to the outlet. Velayati also argued that Iran would act to protect the South Caucasus regardless of Moscow's position, while expressing his belief that Russia opposed the corridor on strategic grounds. NO RETREAT AT HORMUZ — IRAN MUST NOT CONTROL THE WORLD’S ENERGY LIFELINE During a December 2025 meeting with Armenia's ambassador to Tehran, Grigor Hakobyan, Velayati again raised concerns about the proposed route, according to Iran International. The project emerged from a U.S.-brokered diplomatic initiative aimed at ending decades of conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan over Nagorno-Karabakh, an internationally recognized part of Azerbaijan that was controlled for years by ethnic Armenian separatists before Azerbaijani forces retook the territory in 2023. Trump had hosted Pashinyan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev at the White House in 2025, where the two leaders signed a joint declaration intended to advance peace, normalize relations and reopen regional transportation links. The declaration established the basis for the TRIPP initiative, giving Washington a central role in developing infrastructure. Under the implementation framework announced by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan in January, the TRIPP Development Company would oversee development of the infrastructure. TRUMP MEETS KEY IRAN WAR MEDIATOR AS UAE REVEALS MAJOR OIL EXPORT SURGE DESPITE CONFLICT The framework calls for a U.S.-controlled entity to hold a 74% ownership stake in the company, with Armenia retaining 26%. The company would receive development rights for an initial 49-year period, with an option for a further 50-year extension. Under the proposed extension, Armenia's ownership stake would increase to 49%. Armenian authorities would retain jurisdiction over the territory, including responsibility for customs, immigration, law enforcement and border security. The framework also provides for private operators to help facilitate trade and transit, while final customs and security decisions would remain with Armenian authorities. The United States, Armenia and Azerbaijan also announced the launch of trilateral technical planning groups in November to advance the initiative.

articles.title: Auto unions in Pune to go on strike today against bike taxi operation
articles.summary: PUNE: Daily commuters could find it difficult to hail autorickshaws and might be forced to deal with overcharging and fleecing for their basic commutes on
articles.body: PUNE: Daily commuters could find it difficult to hail autorickshaws and might be forced to deal with overcharging and fleecing for their basic commutes on Monday, with several auto unions announcing a one-day strike and demonstration against what they claim to be unabated operations of bike taxis in the city.Pranav Pawar, president of Rickshaw Panchayat, the biggest autorickshaw union in both Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad, said that autos will not operate from 11am to around 2pm.“We are not participating in the strike directly but supporting it. Rickshaw Panchayat and its allied organizations have decided to stage protests at offices of legislators. Demonstrations will commence on Monday in front of the offices of Parvati MLA and transport MoS Madhuri Misal and Pimpri MLA Anna Bansode, who is also deputy speaker of the legislative assembly,” Pawar told TOI.He further accused govt of pursuing a policy to permit bike taxis, claiming this move is threatening to exacerbate the traffic chaos in Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad.“Bike taxis were encroaching upon the already dwindling earnings of auto drivers. Although there is currently no legal authorization for transporting passengers via two-wheelers (bike taxis), the administration lacks the political will to curb this practice. Despite repeated demands, govt remains unwilling to scrap its bike-taxi policy,” Pawar added.The strike is primarily being organised by the Autorickshaw Taxi Federation of India and Maharashtra Rickshaw Panchayat.Baba Kamble, president of the Panchayat, said, “Many unions across the state have agreed to join the strike. Despite having no permission, bike taxis are operating in Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad. The state transport minister admitted that there there are more than 3 lakhs illegal bike taxis operating in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR).""How is it possible that state govt has not been able to stop them despite an FIR issued against one of its operators, Rapido, in Pune?” Kamble added.Keshav Kshirsagar, president of the Baghtoy Rickshawala auto union, also said their members support the strike.“We have always given our support to strikes and protests carried out by any union and will continue to do so. If autos won’t be allowed to operate on Monday and the main organisation is proactive with its demands, we will surely support the same. Bike taxi operations have been further ruining livelihoods of auto drivers, which cannot be acceptable,” he said.On October 18, Pune Regional Transport Office (RTO) office had lodged an FIR against Rapido for bike taxi operations in Pune. At the time, Pune city police commissioner Amitesh Kumar had said that communications had been sent to Apple and Google to remove the bike taxi option from Rapido’s application.However, things didn’t move ahead and later, Uber also began bike taxi operations.For commuters, Monday is expected to be chaotic.“I go to office each day taking an autorickshaw from my place in Lullanagar to my workplace located on JM Road. An auto strike means that we will face multiple issues, ranging from unavailability of autorickshaws to fleecing and overcharging. It will surely be a problem for me and many others,” said Suraj Raju, a private sector employee.Anil Chorde, who lives in Nigdi Pradhikaran, agreed.“Auto drivers and unions are just harassing people. articles.summary: For years now, Willy Wonka has been the face of any chocolate factory owner.
articles.body: For years now, Willy Wonka has been the face of any chocolate factory owner. As children, a chocolate factory was more than just a place of production; it was like the Garden of Eden. We were Adam and Eve, and let's be honest, we would have committed the sin way before Eve if we had been in a paradise like a chocolate factory. But long before fictional chocolate factories captured our imagination, there was a real-life chocolatier whose ambition helped make chocolate more accessible to ordinary people. More than a century later, Hershey is bringing back a small but memorable piece of that history, allowing customers to buy its classic milk chocolate bar for just five cents, its original price when it was first introduced in 1900.As per The Hershey Company, the five-cent chocolate bar will make a one-day comeback on November 25, with limited offers available through Walmart, Amazon and Hershey's own Chocolate World stores. The initiative comes ahead of the release of HERSHEY, an upcoming film based on the life of the company's founder, Milton Hershey, and his wife, Catherine Hershey.Very few of us know that when Milton Hershey introduced the milk chocolate bar in 1900, it was priced at just five cents per piece. At a time when chocolate was considered more of a luxury, reserved for the palates of the rich and nobles, he made milk chocolate more affordable and accessible to ordinary Americans. Hershey's aim was simple: to make every day an occasion to enjoy a good bite of chocolate rather than waiting for a special one, making each day special.The upcoming promotion takes customers back to that original price, though for a day only. It showcases the legacy of the company and the dream of a man who wanted to make chocolate accessible to everyone, rather than limiting it to a privileged few.The man behind the chocolate empireBorn on September 13, 1857, in Pennsylvania, Milton Snavely Hershey did not have an easy journey towards becoming one of America's most recognised confectioners. His interest in making sweets began at a young age, and at just 14, he started working as an apprentice to confectioner Joseph Royer in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. Over the next four years, he learned the art of making candies, experimenting with ingredients and understanding the craft.However, starting a business was not as easy as making sweets. In 1876, after completing his apprenticeship, Hershey started his own candy business in Philadelphia, but it did not work out. He moved to New York and tried his luck there as well, but that business failed too. He then travelled to different places, learning more about the confectionery business. During his stay in Denver, he learned a new way of making caramels using fresh milk, something that would later help him build his business.In 1886, Hershey returned to Lancaster and started the Lancaster Caramel Company. This time, things worked in his favour, and his caramels soon began reaching markets beyond the United States. But Hershey had something else in mind. During the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago, he came across chocolate-making machinery. Naturally fascinated by the process, he bought the equipment and started experimenting with chocolate himself.A year later, in 1894, he started the Hershey Chocolate Company as part of his already existing caramel business. By 1900, he had sold the Lancaster Caramel Company and decided to focus entirely on chocolate. The man who had once struggled to keep his small candy businesses running was now ready to build something much bigger.How Hershey made chocolate accessible to everyoneFor Hershey, chocolate was not meant to remain something that only a few could afford. At the time, milk chocolate was largely considered a luxury, with much of it coming from Europe and being sold at high prices. He wanted ordinary Americans to enjoy it too, and for that, he needed to find a way to make it in larger quantities without making it expensive.He spent years experimenting with milk chocolate and eventually worked out a formula that could be produced on a much larger scale. In 1903, he began building a large chocolate factory in Derry Township, Pennsylvania, a place that would later grow into the town of Hershey. The factory began production in 1905, giving him the means to produce chocolate in large quantities and bring it to a much wider market.The introduction of the Hershey's Milk Chocolate Bar in 1900 had already marked an important step towards this ambition. By combining large-scale production with an affordable price, Hershey helped turn chocolate from an occasional luxury into an everyday indulgence for American consumers. The familiar five-cent price became central to this identity, making the chocolate bar accessible to a much wider audience.This was not just the beginning of a successful chocolate business; it was the foundation of a brand that would eventually become part of American popular culture.Now, more than a century later, his journey is set to come to the big screen. A real-life Willy Wonka is set to reach audiences through the upcoming film HERSHEY. The film explores not just the making of a chocolate empire but also the man and the personal story behind it, including his relationship with his wife, Catherine Hershey. And as the company brings back its original five-cent price for a day, the timing offers a reminder that sometimes the story behind a familiar treat can be just as interesting as the treat itself.You use AI every day. articles.title: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
articles.summary: Nine people are dead in the attack, with rescue efforts ongoing to find those still missing from the residential building.
articles.body:
A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer after 14 hours, in overnight Russian strikes on Dymer, in the Kyiv region, that killed nine people, Ukrainian officials have said.

The attack occurred in the early hours of Sunday. A 79-year-old woman was also rescued alive from the collapsed building, Kyiv's regional head Tymur Tkachenko said.

A strike on a private home in Bila Tserkva killed one more person and set the building ablaze, he added.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 wounded in a separate strike on Vyshneve, also in the Kyiv region, that hit a grocery store on Sunday.

Ukrainian authorities said the boy in Dymer is in stable condition and was taken to hospital, and have thanked everyone involved in saving his life.

Zelensky and Ukraine's national police also confirmed the rescue of the boy.

Response teams including police, explosive technicians, dog handlers and medics are continuing with rescue efforts.

In a telegram post, Tkachenko said the 79-year-old woman rescued from the rubble was receiving treatment in hospital.

Earlier he said six people were injured in the attack, while others were still missing.

Zelensky said more than 130 people are involved in emergency operations at the scene, and that they will continue until they have "complete information about every single person".

Sending his condolences to the families and loved ones of those killed, he said the strike struck the residential building, "practically blowing a section of it to smithereens".

Zelensky added that "rescue efforts are complicated by constant new air raid alerts and renewed threats".

The strike hit the building at 05:00 local time, when families were still asleep, Ukraine's minister of internal affairs Ivan Vyhivskyi said.

More than 70 strikes have been launched across 10 Ukrainian regions as of Sunday evening, Vyhivskyi added.

In his video address posted online, Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 injured in a strike on an "ordinary grocery store" in Vyshneve.

Tkachenko previously said two other people were killed and eight wounded in the Vyshneve attack.

Russia also struck a power substation in the Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukraine's Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky said in a post on X.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

articles.title: Warren Beatty and Annette Bening sold their Los Angeles mansion for $6.7 million in 2012; the new owners spent $5 million renovating the nine-bedroom estate, which is now listed for nearly $15 million
articles.summary: The Los Angeles mansion custom-built for Warren Beatty and Annette Bening has hit the market again. The 10,594 sq. ft.
articles.body: The Los Angeles mansion custom-built for Warren Beatty and Annette Bening has hit the market again. The 10,594 sq. ft. mansion, with seven bedrooms and twelve bathrooms, is asking $14.995 million, according to a report by Mansion Global. Cory Weiss and Jacob Greene of Douglas Elliman have listed the gated Mulholland Drive compound, which recently underwent a $5 million renovation.The current owners bought the house in 2012 for $6.7 million from the Hollywood couple, according to PropertyShark records. The buyers are hoteliers.A home built for Hollywood royaltyThe house was built in 1992 for actor-filmmaker Warren Beatty and actress Annette Bening, the same year they got married. The couple spent their early years of marriage building a life together and raising their four children, including the youngest, Ella Beatty, who recently played Lizzie Borden in Netflix's ‘Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story’. The pair's relationship grew during the making of ‘Bugsy’, the 1991 gangster film in which both starred.Warren Beatty and Annette Bening are nothing short of a power couple. Beatty has received 14 Academy Award nominations. In 1982, he received the Best Director award. He has also won three Golden Globe Awards. Bening, on the other hand, has received five Oscar nominations, including Best Actress for 1999’s ‘American Beauty’, for which she also won a Golden Globe. This Mulholland mansion has seen it all: their marriage, their flourishing careers and their family. The couple kept the house for about two decades before selling it.They sold the mansion in 2012In 2012, the current owners purchased the property and made some modern renovations to the Mediterranean-style house, ‘without taking away its history’. ‘They really opened everything up, modernised the finishes and took it from a traditional Mediterranean to something much more contemporary,’ Weiss told the outlet. The most noticeable change is in Beatty's old office, which is now a 17-seat theatre named after him. The owners kept his original drop-down projection screen and installed it in the redesigned living room. The listing highlights the theatre by name: the Warren Beatty Theater.‘A completely private, gated compound on approximately 1.1 acres, this seven-bedroom former celebrity estate brings together three structures, sweeping views and a Hollywood history on one of Los Angeles's most iconic roads,’ the listing describes.The compound spans approximately 1.1 acres and includes a separate guest house. A dramatic arched entry leads to a sweeping staircase, large living and dining rooms, and a dedicated wine room. The glass walls bring in the beauty of the hills and city lights. The primary suite has a fireplace, a sitting area, a large dressing room and a terrace overlooking the hills.Outside, terraces surround a heated in-ground pool. A private tennis court sits on the grounds, and trails connect the property to the area near TreePeople, the Los Angeles urban forest non-profit. Weiss pitched the property as a rare setting inside the city. ‘You’re getting a full compound right in the middle of Los Angeles. You’re minutes from Beverly Hills, the Valley and some of the best private schools in Los Angeles. You have everything around you, but once you’re on the property, you feel like you’re somewhere completely different,’ the listing agent said.The listing leans heavily on privacy and the estate's Hollywood history. One of the attractions beyond the elaborate mansion is certainly the fact that the Hollywood couple kept the house for two decades before selling it in 2012. After spending nearly $5 million on renovations, the current owners are now putting it back on the market.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Trump dares Iran to breach US port blockade as Tehran reportedly readies 14 oil tankers
articles.summary: Iran reportedly positioned 14 tankers at Kharg Island to breach the U.S. blockade, as President Donald Trump dared Tehran to test American naval forces in the Gulf.
articles.body: Reports that Iran plans to send more than a dozen tankers through the U.S. blockade of its ports raised fears of a wider conflict Sunday, as a maritime security expert warned of a risky confrontation and President Donald Trump dared Tehran to test American forces deployed across the Gulf. "I hope they do, they'll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy," Trump told Fox News chief foreign correspondent Trey Yingst when asked whether Iran would attempt to breach the blockade, first imposed in April. The warning came as reports indicated Iran was preparing a convoy of tankers to breach the blockade from Kharg Island, a critical oil export hub. TRUMP DETAILS SWEEPING 'ALL OR NOTHING' BLOCKADE OF STRAIT OF HORMUZ AFTER FAILED IRAN TALKS Maritime security experts warned the vessels could face U.S. naval forces right across the Indian Ocean, while the Institute for the Study of War cautioned that an attempted breakout could perhaps trigger a wider war. The reported operation would involve tankers sailing from Kharg Island, which handles most of Iran's crude oil exports, toward the Gulf of Oman and with crews reportedly assigned to the vessels and Iranian flags raised ahead of a possible attempt to breach the blockade. Charlie Brown, a senior adviser to United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI) and maritime sanctions enforcement expert, dismissed the reported operation as "propaganda" and said the plan was unlikely to succeed if ever attempted. "This supposed plan by the Iranians to suddenly deploy 14 vessels to try to breach the blockade in a convoy — it's farcical," Brown told Fox News Digital on Sunday. "The blockade is enforced not merely as a line that is crossed, but the ability of the United States Navy to enforce this blockade extends across the entire Indian Ocean and beyond." BLOCKADE 101: AMERICAN SEA POWER ON DISPLAY AS TRUMP CORNERS IRAN AND WARNS OFF CHINA "If ships try to get out of the area that is managed by the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet, the U.S. Navy's 7th Fleet is the next area command that has responsibility over the Indian Ocean," he said. "And they have ships and aircraft that are there right now, and they'll just take up the mission." The potential confrontation comes amid rising maritime tensions. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported Sunday that a tanker was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman but did not identify the vessel or connect it to the reported Iranian convoy. "UKMTO has received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman," the agency said in an advisory. "Vessels are advised to consider the latest maritime security information and maintain awareness of the evolving operational environment." The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) also warned Iran could attempt to break the blockade within days as mounting economic pressure leaves Tehran with few options. "Iran's deteriorating economic situation is increasingly dire, which is forcing Iranian officials to reckon with the necessity of breaking the US blockade," the institute said in an update. The assessment followed a Nov. 20 report by Hamshahri, a Tehran municipality-affiliated outlet, claiming Iran had positioned 14 tankers at Kharg Island to breach the blockade. TRUMP BLOCKADE SQUEEZING IRAN SO HARD REGIME MAY BE DUMPING OIL INTO GULF, EXPERTS SAY "Attempting to run the blockade would expose Iran to significant risk that ranges from the destruction of a tanker fleet at minimum to possibly resuming a larger-scale conflict with the United States, or both," the institute said. "Iran's willingness to accept these risks demonstrates the degree to which the regime views the current economic situation as both dire and unsustainable." Brown, however, questioned whether Tehran would send the tankers, suggesting the reported operation was an attempt to project defiance rather than a viable strategy. "This supposed run of the blockade by several Iranian ships that's discussed is most likely propaganda — another one of a series of similar propaganda statements that don't turn out to be true and are easily debunked," he said. Brown also disputed reports that the tankers were loaded and preparing to depart, citing satellite monitoring of Kharg Island. "We carefully watched Kharg Island loading by satellite imagery, and there's really no indication that there's been any significant loading there in quite some time." Brown said coordinating a 14-vessel convoy would also pose major logistical challenges, requiring lead and trailing ships, coordinated communications and procedures for responding to U.S. military orders. Civilian crews could face significant danger if they refused orders to stop, he warned. TRUMP WARNS OF NEW STRIKES AGAINST IRAN AFTER NEW YEAR, CALLS NEGOTIATORS ‘PROFESSIONAL TAP DANCERS’ "They would obviously be going into an area of great risk, and they would have to decide whether to comply with the instructions to stop or face action," Brown said. In a Nov. 18 advisory, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) warned that ships receiving Iranian cargo through ship-to-ship transfers could face interception or seizure, extending the blockade beyond vessels departing Iranian ports, Reuters reported. Brown said U.S. forces would likely contact the tankers by radio from Navy ships or aircraft and order them to stop. Refusal could trigger an escalated military response. He said the Navy could transfer responsibility between regional commands, making it difficult for Iranian tankers to escape by sailing farther into the Indian Ocean. "There's an administrative boundary, a geographic boundary between the 5th Fleet and the 7th Fleet, between CENTCOM and INDOPACOM," Brown said. "But the U.S. Navy is a global Navy, and they're able to handle these transfers of responsibility when a target or ship of interest crosses that boundary." Brown said U.S. forces have the ships, aircraft and procedures to intercept multiple vessels at once, while the open waters of the Indian Ocean offer more room to maneuver than the narrow Strait of Hormuz. "It's a mission of the United States, not merely a mission in CENTCOM," Brown said. "So they have the forces in place." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "So if they do try to make an attempt with multiple ships, I'm quite confident all or most — probably all — would be interdicted," he added.

articles.title: Watch: Russian warship hit by suspected Ukrainian drones at Benghazi naval base, bursts into flames
articles.summary: A suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack struck a Russian navy warship at the port of Benghazi in eastern Libya, triggering an explosion and fire and
articles.body: A suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack struck a Russian navy warship at the port of Benghazi in eastern Libya, triggering an explosion and fire and leaving the vessel partially submerged.The ship, identified as the Russian corvette Merkury, was docked at the port to refuel and take on supplies under a cooperation agreement between Moscow and the eastern-based Libyan administration. Satellite imagery shared by imagery provider Vantor showed that most of the vessel had capsized and sunk, with only its bow visible above water. Smoke and debris were also seen around the ship.Two Libyan military officials told the Associated Press that Ukrainian sea drones had been launched at the warship from a base operated by Ukrainian forces in western Libya. At least four drones were intercepted, while two struck the vessel, they said. Neither Ukraine nor Russia has commented on the attack.Meanwhile, local sources told Al Jazeera that an unknown number of Libyan and Russian nationals were killed. They also claimed the vessel was carrying weapons, ammunition and drones. Residents reportedly saw three drones attack the ship. These claims have not been publicly confirmed.The eastern-based Libyan administration said the fire had been brought under control and launched a joint investigation with Russia to establish the source of the attack. It condemned the suspected strike as a violation of Libya's sovereignty and a threat to maritime safety."The Libyan government will not allow Libyan ports, territory or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts," it said, adding that Libya was "not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war".Earlier, in a separate incident on Sunday evening, a sea drone struck a Malta-flagged commercial vessel off Benghazi. The eastern administration's Health Ministry said all crew members injured in the attack had been rescued and were receiving treatment. Almasar television reported that naval and air forces destroyed at least 12 other sea drones off the Mediterranean city.The western-based Libyan government also expressed concern over attempts to involve the country's ports and civilian facilities in external conflicts.Ukraine's 'presence' in LibyaThe suspected attack comes amid reports of Ukrainian military and intelligence personnel operating in western Libya. Middle East security and defence expert Tallha Abdulrazaq told Al Jazeera that Ukrainian intelligence services were most likely behind the strike."There was a lot of reporting on the tail end of last year about there being a deal between the Ukrainian intelligence services and the Tripolitan government to establish a Ukrainian military and intelligence presence there," he said."In exchange, the Tripoli government would get Ukrainian military expertise," he added.Libya has remained divided between rival administrations since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime leader Muammar Gaddafi in 2011. A UN-recognised government is based in Tripoli, while a rival administration controls the east.The head of the eastern-based Libyan government, Osama Hammad, has sought an international investigation, asking the UN to examine whether the drones were launched from western Libya and verify reports of Ukrainian experts operating in the country.You use AI every day. articles.body: A video game robbery rarely leads to a life-changing moment outside the screen. However, MrBeast found a way to make it happen. The YouTube star offered real cash for every dollar his longtime cameraman, Tareq Salameh, could steal in GTA 6. What began as a race against police, security guards and a ticking clock soon became a personal mission. Salameh wanted to use the opportunity to give something back to his mother. After an intense 60-minute challenge, he walked away with approximately $44,000 for her, turning a gaming stunt into an emotional family moment.Tareq Salameh fights setbacks in MrBeast’s GTA 6 challengeThe challenge featured in MrBeast Gaming's November 20 video, titled 'Whatever You Steal in GTA 6, You Keep!' The timing also added to the excitement, as the video arrived just one day after Rockstar Games released GTA 6.Salameh entered the challenge with one clear goal. He wanted to earn as much as possible for his mother, who had supported him throughout his life.'I'm, like, literally not joking. I'm doing this for my mom. I don't care how high it is,' he said.Salameh, who was born in Saudi Arabia to Palestinian-Jordanian parents, moved to the United States as a child. He credited his mother with helping him adjust to his new surroundings, including teaching him English.'She taught me everything. She taught me how to speak English. You know what I mean? I love my mom,' he said.However, the challenge came with strict conditions. Every dollar stolen in GTA 6 counted towards the real-life payout, but getting arrested or killed would erase his entire balance. He also could not deposit his money in a bank to protect it.His final task was equally difficult. He had to get aboard an aircraft and take off before the 60-minute timer expired.MrBeast’s $44,000 GTA 6 challenge ends with an emotional payoffSalameh initially built a strong balance by robbing a jewellery store, collecting more than $5,000. However, an attempted robbery at a loan store in Little Cuba nearly ended his chances. Armed security guards killed his character, wiping out everything he had earned.Instead of giving up, he returned to the challenge and started building his total again. He stole vehicles, sold them for cash, broke into a Fleeca bank vault and targeted more businesses.Eventually, his earnings crossed $44,000. But the biggest obstacle was still ahead.With police chasing him and time running out, Salameh hijacked a bus at the airport and rushed towards a passenger aircraft. MrBeast urged him to forget about earning more money and focus on escaping before the deadline.Salameh managed to get airborne just in time, securing the promised payout. His mother's reaction made the achievement even more meaningful, as she called him 'the best son ever'.While the video also featured a promotion for financial technology platform Step, the challenge's emotional centre remained Salameh's decision to use his gaming skills to reward the person who had done so much for him.For him, the biggest win was never the money inside GTA 6. articles.summary: US CBP data shows 1,389 unaccompanied Indian children taken into custody since FY23; numbers fell sharply as enforcement rose and deportations sped up.
articles.body: AHMEDABAD: The anti-immigration crackdown in US has swept 1,389 unaccompanied Indian children into custody since America’s FY23. These children have not been repatriated.However, the unyielding drive against immigrants has reduced the number of unaccompanied Indian children found in US: 730 in FY23, 517 in FY24, 91 in FY25, 51 in FY26, and two in Oct 2026, the first month of US FY27.The data is from US Customs and Border Protection (USCBP).The decline mirrors the trend for unaccompanied children of all nationalities. US authorities recorded 1.1 lakh unaccompanied children in FY24, 29,584 in FY25, and 9,190 in FY26. In Oct 2026, 722 children were found unaccompanied.People familiar with immigration networks in US said the decline could partly be linked to stricter enforcement and faster deportations. Earlier, minors were allegedly used as ‘green card bringers’ to help parents or relatives strengthen their chances of obtaining legal status.This practice is reportedly becoming less common as authorities swiftly deport those caught.A businessman from Kadi, who was deported from US in 2012, said his 17-year-old son, who has been living in Texas since he was 12, is now afraid to attend his asylum hearings.“He thinks he will be caught and deported to India. He has been secretly working at a gas station and living with members of a religious sect,” the businessman said.The trend comes even as Indians continue to feature among the top nationalities attempting illegal entry into US. articles.title: An Alaska dentist reported $36,960 in income and was ordered to pay $697.94 a month for four children, but judges found he understated his earnings and raised support to $3,780; the state's top court upheld the increase
articles.summary: A financial disclosure that initially resulted in a father’s monthly child support payment being less than $700 became the focus of a legal fight over
articles.body: A financial disclosure that initially resulted in a father’s monthly child support payment being less than $700 became the focus of a legal fight over income transparency and parental responsibility. A dentist in Alaska claimed his earnings were $36,960, but it turned out he was making substantially more, which led to a dramatic hike in child support payments for his four children. The Alaska Supreme Court has now upheld the new order, ruling that parents cannot take advantage of protections against retroactive child support changes to benefit from knowingly underreporting their income.Legal dispute over income differenceAccording to the Alaska Supreme Court’s decision in Bowen v. Ray, 2 No. S-18430 (Nov. 20, 2026), Doug Bowen is a pediatric dentist and member of the Alaska Army National Guard who separated from his wife, Deana Ray, in March 2022. Two months later, Ray filed for divorce.During the course of the proceedings, both parties submitted financial information to determine child support. Bowen reported earning $36,960 a year. In January 2023, the Palmer Superior Court ordered Bowen to pay $697.94 a month for their four children, who are mostly in Ray’s care.But Ray later disputed the calculation, saying Bowen had not included several sources of income in his financial disclosures.Documents reveal substantially larger earningsIn describing the proceedings, the Alaska Supreme Court said Ray submitted tax documents showing Bowen earned about $183,688 from his private dental practice in 2021. She also submitted employment records indicating he started with Southcentral Foundation in September 2022 with an annual salary of about $176,000.The higher-paying employment was supported by Bowen’s own testimony at the divorce trial. His pay records showed gross monthly earnings of about $13,266, plus a $17,247 sign-on bonus.The lower court also considered business deductions claimed by Bowen, among them accelerated depreciation. It found the deductions were not enough to justify discounting his much higher income in setting child support.Increase in monthly payments for back payIn September 2023, the Superior Court found that Bowen's income exceeded the applicable Alaska child support guideline amount of $126,000. This increased his monthly obligation from $697.94 to $3,780 effective October 1, 2022, when he had started his higher paying job.Bowen appealed, claiming the increase violated Alaska Civil Rule 90.3, which generally bars retroactive changes in child support obligations.The Alaska Supreme Court rejected that argument, noting that the restriction was not intended to protect people who knowingly misrepresent their financial circumstances.Supreme Court dismisses retroactivity argumentIn a Nov. 20, 2026, decision, the Alaska Supreme Court ruled that the state’s restrictions on retroactively changing child support do not extend to instances of intentional financial misrepresentation.The judges said the original order was based on misleading income information and allowing the lower payment to stand would undermine the purpose of child support protections. The court noted the rules were designed to ensure children receive appropriate financial support and not to shield parents who knowingly provide false financial disclosures.The Supreme Court therefore affirmed the lower court’s decision to apply the higher payments as of October 2022, when Bowen began his higher-paying job.Property dispute adds another dimensionThe appeal also concerned Silver Springs, a commercial property legally owned by Bowen’s parents, which they purchased for his dental practice.The lower court determined that during the marriage, Bowen had been paying his parents about $2,000 each month, with the understanding that eventually he would own the property.Bowen argued the payments were for rent and other unpaid debts, but the Alaska Supreme Court ruled there was enough evidence to support the lower court decision that payments had created an equity interest in the marital estate.The judges therefore agreed with the ruling that that equity was to be treated as marital property subject to division in the divorce.Earlier support adjustment separateThe Alaska Supreme Court also noted a later order, issued in February 2024, lowered Bowen’s monthly child support obligation to $1,562.81 after a change in the custody arrangement between the parents. But that adjustment wasn’t included in the appeal.The state's highest court, in its final ruling on the matter, upheld the lower court's conclusions on the divisions of marital property and the child support computations, leaving unchanged the decisions that were contested.Image Courtesy: Google GeminiYou use AI every day. articles.title: UK weather: Will it snow this week?
articles.summary: A battle ground is becoming established across the UK, milder air across the southwest and cold arctic air elsewhere
articles.body:
The UK is in the grip of the coldest spell of autumn so far, but will it result in snow?

Mild Atlantic air that arrived in the south-west of the UK over the weekend is pushing eastwards, coming up against colder Arctic air.

In this setup, the meteorological ingredients for snow are in place; however, there remains uncertainty in where the boundary between the cold and mild air will sit.

Even small shifts in temperature could make a significant difference to what falls from the sky and, crucially, the chances of snow.

A clash between the air masses is already underway, as weather systems arrived from the Atlantic overnight into Sunday, bringing milder air with them.

The coming days will see the UK caught between lingering cold air, held in place by a dominant area of high pressure over Norway, and milder, wetter conditions associated with Sunday's weather fronts.

For many, the main hazards will be freezing fog and icy stretches, particularly where skies clear overnight.

Further west, rain could still bring a risk of disruption, while uncertainty remains over the potential for snow.

The key question is whether the cold air can hold its ground or whether milder Atlantic conditions will steadily push eastwards.

Mild in the south-west, but colder air dominates elsewhere

Monday will begin on a cold note, with temperatures widely below freezing, bringing frost along with patches of ice and freezing fog.

Blue skies and just a few fair-weather clouds will follow the frost.

Any patchy fog will clear, but with winds a little fresher than on Sunday, temperatures will reach 8 to 10C.

Meanwhile, Sunday's bands of rain will gradually weaken over southwest England and Wales, where conditions will remain grey, damp and blustery.

At times, cloud and light rain will also spread into Northern Ireland.

By midweek, the battleground will shift further eastwards.

Early on Tuesday, the weather front - which by then will mainly consist of a band of cloud - will have edged further east.

As a result, it will be a little less chilly to start the day, but cloudier for most.

Another, more active weather front will quickly follow, moving eastwards across Northern Ireland on Tuesday morning.

It is then forecast to spread into northern and western England, Wales and much of Scotland through the day, bringing the first chance of snow to the Highlands and Grampians.

Tuesday night and Wednesday will be dominated by cloudy skies, with weather fronts bringing rain at times.

The situation could be complicated by another area of low pressure developing in the English Channel.

This would not only bring more rain to the south but also strengthen easterly winds, which would begin to push the cold air back westwards.

articles.body: DHAKA: Bangladesh's key export-earning ready-made garment sector suffered $428 million in production losses during 18 days of unrest, while buyers shifted orders worth another $254 million to competing countries, a preliminary industry survey found. The numbers, industry insiders said, were "worrying" for the world's second-largest apparel exporter. Bangladesh is behind only China and its closest competitors are Vietnam, Turkiye, India and Italy.Meanwhile, PM Tarique Rahman proposed dialogue with "anti-fascist political parties" amid recent political violence, and massive protests and shutdowns by garment workers, demanding increase in wages, since Oct.Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) Sunday said its survey covered the period from Nov 1-18 and collected responses from 317 garment factories that reported production disruptions due to the prevailing instability and various operational disruptions. "The affected factories incurred production losses amounting to $428 million in free-on-board (FOB) value during the period," it said. "The losses were compounded by difficulties in meeting shipment deadlines, leaving many export orders at risk. To retain orders and meet delivery commitments, factories were forced to resort to costly air shipments, offer substantial price discounts and, in some cases, face order cancellations," BGMEA said.Without naming the competing countries, the survey said international buyers had shifted 59 million pieces of confirmed garment orders, worth $254 million, to other countries. articles.title: At least 16 children suffered lead poisoning in homes owned by a New York landlord; after he failed to obey a $310,000 court settlement to remove the hazards, the state has permanently banned him from renting properties
articles.summary: A landlord’s failure to address a hidden danger inside homes has now cost him his place in New York’s rental housing market.
articles.body: A landlord’s failure to address a hidden danger inside homes has now cost him his place in New York’s rental housing market. At least 16 children suffered lead poisoning while living in properties owned by Syracuse landlord William D’Angelo, whose repeated failure to eliminate hazardous lead paint conditions has prompted state authorities to take decisive action. Following violations of an earlier court settlement, D’Angelo must sell his remaining rental properties and will be permanently barred from owning or managing residential rentals across New York.Court action follows repeated violationsAccording to the New York State Attorney General’s Office, Attorney General Letitia James announced the agreement after D’Angelo failed to comply with a February 2024 court-approved settlement worth $310,000. The agreement had required him to address lead hazards at 18 designated priority properties by December 2025.The latest settlement resolves a contempt proceeding initiated by the Attorney General’s Office in August 2026 after repeated warnings failed to secure compliance.The original legal action dates back to 2023, when the Attorney General’s Office, Onondaga County and the City of Syracuse sued D’Angelo. An investigation identified approximately 336 lead-based paint violations across nearly two dozen properties, with at least 16 children recording elevated blood lead levels.More concerns were raised about unsafe repairsD'Angelo paid restitution to affected families under the 2024 settlement. Later, his efforts to remove remaining threats stalled.A June 2026 inspection by Syracuse city officials identified continuing violations. Investigators also discovered that D’Angelo had undertaken lead-related repair work himself without employing an Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)-certified contractor, following an approved work plan or securing the required independent monitoring.The court subsequently determined that he had violated the original judgment. Although some violations have since been corrected, lead hazards remain at 10 of the 18 priority properties, according to the Attorney General’s Office.New agreement puts properties under scrutinyUnder the latest agreement, D’Angelo must sell all his remaining rental properties within 180 days. Every prospective buyer will require approval from the Attorney General’s Office in coordination with Syracuse and Onondaga County authorities.Buyers acquiring properties with unresolved lead hazards must commit to completing remediation through EPA-certified professionals. Repairs must be finished within 60 days of purchase for occupied homes and 120 days for vacant properties.New owners cannot collect rent from existing tenants or rent out vacant units until all identified lead hazards have been eliminated. If an occupied property remains unsold after 90 days, D’Angelo must arrange and finance the necessary repairs himself using certified contractors and an approved monitor.Financial penalties and a wider public health concernThe agreement imposes a penalty of $100 per day for each property where deadlines or other requirements are breached. D’Angelo could also face a $37,500 penalty for every property where he performs lead remediation himself instead of hiring certified professionals. State Supreme Court Justice Joseph Lamendola has warned that further violations could result in additional consequences, including imprisonment.Finger Lakes Daily News reported that D’Angelo owned or managed at least 48 Syracuse rental properties containing 116 units over three decades. All were constructed before 1940, making them presumed to contain lead-based paint.The Attorney General’s Office has also highlighted the wider scale of the problem. During the first half of 2026, 9.4 per cent of Syracuse children tested had elevated blood lead levels. In 2025, testing identified elevated levels in 158 Black children, compared with 56 white children.The latest agreement marks another step in New York's efforts to address childhood lead exposure. Once D’Angelo completes the sale of his remaining properties, his removal from the state's residential rental market will be permanent.Image Courtesy: Google GeminiYou use AI every day. articles.title: US spy chief confirms probe into Nvidia-linked chip supply network involving Alice Huang, China
articles.summary: US spy chief Jay Clayton has confirmed that investigations into Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and her company, Megaspeed, are ongoing amid the
articles.body: US spy chief Jay Clayton has confirmed that investigations into Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and her company, Megaspeed, are ongoing amid the controversy surrounding former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The confirmation comes after reports suggesting Alice Huang remained in contact with an official from China's ministry of state security for more than a year.The probes are linked to allegations that the company was part of a network involved in supplying Nvidia-powered servers to Chinese customers.In an interview with Fox News, Clayton said investigations into both Huang and the company were progressing alongside regulatory proceedings. He also indicated that Nvidia's board of directors was expected to examine the matter."There is an investigation into her company, and there is an investigation into her. That is going to play out," Clayton said."Also, I fully expect that the board of directors of Nvidia is looking into this situation. You know, that would be responsible; that's what the American people want to hear from them. And there are—are regulatory proceedings going on. The American people will get answers regarding this matter," he added.The investigations come amid controversy surrounding former Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang, who resigned on November 12 following reports of an alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive suspected by US intelligence agencies of having links to Chinese intelligence.Jensen Huang had acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife. Nvidia, however, said it had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets had been compromised.Nvidia board chairman Harvey Jones said directors had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and did not intend to reinstate him. Chief financial officer Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO. Huang had said he would be honoured to return if the board considered it in the company's interest.This comes after a Wall Street Journal (WSJ) report, published on Saturday, detailed the alleged role of Chinese national Li Ming in a network of companies supplying computing capacity to Chinese customers through Southeast Asia.According to the report, Li, 52, was closely involved in Megaspeed's operations and major business decisions. Singapore prosecutors charged him and others with fraud in February 2025 over the alleged transshipment of servers containing Nvidia chips. Megaspeed was not named in those charges.The WSJ reported that Li worked with Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, and that the three helped establish a network of partners across Southeast Asia. Megaspeed subsequently joined Nvidia's cloud partner programme in November 2023, gaining priority access to its latest chips, the newspaper reported.The report also alleged that some servers were transferred to Shanghai-based Century Litong in violation of US export controls. Nvidia placed Megaspeed on an internal "no sell" list in June 2025.Megaspeed has maintained that its business was legitimate and lawful, adding that Alice Huang left in August 2025. Singapore authorities reportedly questioned her over suspected chip smuggling and barred her from re-entering the country.The WSJ further reported that a new venture, Novagate Cloud, had received at least $300 million worth of Nvidia-chip hardware in Malaysia during the first five months of 2026.Meanwhile, The New York Times reported on Sunday that Alice Huang remained in contact with an official from China's state security ministry for more than a year, from spring 2025 to autumn 2026, during her alleged affair with Jensen Huang.The report further said that US intelligence agencies had gathered evidence suggesting that Alice's business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, had also worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. The extent and timing of both individuals' alleged contacts with the agency had not been previously reported, the newspaper said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Maharashtra drought may be worse than 1972, says state agriculture minister Dattatray Bharne
articles.summary: Maharashtra may face drought worse than 1972 as rabi sowing drops to 14.29 lakh hectares; minister warns challenges until June amid El Niño, low rain.
articles.body: PUNE: State agriculture minister Dattatray Bharne, citing the sharp decline in rabi sowing this year, warned on Sunday that the state was now likely to see a drought much more severe than the one that hit in 1972.According to data from the state Agriculture Department, farmers have so far completed rabi sowing on just 14.29 lakh hectares, significantly lower than the 47.29 lakh hectares recorded during the 1972 drought.The decline, Bharne said, was a matter of serious concern because it had happened despite vast improvements in the state’s irrigation systems over the last 50 years.“Considering the improvements, the area under Rabi sowing should ideally have increased. But it has declined significantly compared to 1972, when Maharashtra had one of the worst droughts in its history. The reduced sowing area indicates this year’s drought could be more severe than the 1972 drought,” Bharne said.The sharp reduction in Rabi sowing could further affect agricultural production, farmers’ incomes and water availability for both farming and domestic consumption.Bharne said the state govt would have to prepare for a challenging situation that could continue until next June.“Due to El Niño conditions, the state received below-normal rainfall. Barring July, there was hardly any rain. Now, considering available water storage, we need to plan until June next year. It is a challenging time for everyone, but the state and central governments continue to stand by every citizen of our state,” the minister said.The opposition criticised the state govt, claiming it had failed to handle the drought situation. State NCP (SP) president Shashikant Shinde said, “Even after announcing a drought in the state two months ago, there has been no announcement of a relief package by the Centre. The state government is also not following up with the Centre to seek assistance. Farmer suicides have already started in Maharashtra but the state government has not taken any measures to prevent them.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Pune | Silver Rate in Pune | Bank Holidays in Pune | Public Holidays in Pune | Petrol Price in Pune | Diesel Price in Pune | CNG Price in Pune | LPG Price in PuneStay updated with the latest Pune news. articles.title: India has quantum talent. Now it needs labs
articles.summary: Vedika Khemani says India has excellent researchers and bright students, but its experimental science infrastructure, particularly in quantum physics,
articles.body: Vedika Khemani says India has excellent researchers and bright students, but its experimental science infrastructure, particularly in quantum physics, remains far behind what is needed to compete globally.Khemani, a theoretical physicist and associate professor at Stanford University and winner of the Infosys Prize 2024 in physical sciences, split her sabbatical between two institutions. She gave a public lecture at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS) in Bengaluru as part of a conference marking 100 years of quantum mechanics, and then spent two weeks at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (IACS) in Kolkata, the city she had grown up in before moving to the US for undergraduate studies.She chose IACS because researchers there were working close to her own field, non-equilibrium dynamics. Her field sits at the frontier of condensed-matter and quantum physics. Much of conventional physics describes systems in thermal equilibrium, where temperature and pressure can be used to characterise the state of matter. Khemani studies systems of interacting quantum particles that never settle into such equilibrium.That can allow phenomena that conventional statistical mechanics would rule out. Her own doctoral work produced the idea of a time crystal, an exotic phase of matter that was once thought to be prohibited by equilibrium thermodynamics.The IACS researchers she worked with were studying another unusual phenomenon they call dynamical freezing. Their systems also appear not to reach thermal equilibrium, but in a setting quite different from the one Khemani had studied. “There’s no reason to believe that they should exist, but they’ve found this phenomenon,” she says. She and the researchers worked together to understand how it could happen and what the underlying physics might be.Engineered quantum systems used to build quantum computers are also systems that need to be controlled dynamically. If researchers can find ways to prevent information from leaking away into the environment, such behaviour could eventually help make quantum devices more robust and stable.Strong in theory, poor in experimental physicsKhemani says while there are excellent scientists in Indian institutions, they are generally under-recognised. She found the students at IACS curious, bright and capable of engaging seriously with difficult questions.She was particularly impressed by ICTS (part of Tata Institute of Fundamental Research - TIFR) in Bengaluru. “ICTS is world class. They have an international visitor program for scientists. They make everything seamless for such visitors, there's even housing. They have year-round conferences. It’s like attending a conference anywhere in the world,” she says.But she sees a major structural gap. Experimental physics, she says, is “very far lagging” in India, particularly in quantum science. Theory can often be done with a laptop and ideas. Experiments require expensive equipment, reliable infrastructure and funding that can be counted on over many years.In quantum laboratories, even a minor electrical fluctuation can destroy months of carefully prepared experimental work. Researchers need clean rooms, stable power and highly controlled environments. Stanford ensures that. India, Khemani says, needs similar infrastructure if it wants to compete in building quantum hardware, not just producing theoretical papers.Chinese investment in quantum science, she says, has enabled the country to produce research at a level that is beginning to challenge leading US institutions.The US model itself, she notes, relies heavily on govt funding for basic science. Companies such as Google, Amazon and quantum startups are now investing, but much of the fundamental science that enabled these commercial efforts was built through govt-backed research over many years. China is also making large govt investments in quantum.The researchers at IACS (Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science, Kolkata) were curious and bright, and I got good questions during my talk. Arnab Das is the faculty member there. I also worked with two students – Sagnik Chaudhuri and Anirban Das – and a student who used to be at IACS and who’s now a postdoc in Europe, Asmi Halder. I’ve had very good experiences working with them. Vedika Khemani, Associate Professor, Stanford UniversityFearless legend or grounded realist?
